purpose: Curated dated vendor CVE and GHSA security advisories for product-specific categories. Every entry retains the original publication date, and GHSA-only entries are not counted as CVEs. Whitecap public service descriptions do not establish that any product or affected version is deployed.

advisories.title: Progress Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX unsafe persistence deserialization
advisories.summary: RadPersistenceManager and RadDockLayout can deserialize attacker-controlled cookie-based state in affected configurations, potentially enabling remote code execution. Part of the vendor's critical chained RCE bulletin.
advisories.affected: Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX 2026.2.519 and earlier when vulnerable cookie-based persistence configuration is enabled.
advisories.remediation: Upgrade Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX to 2026.2.708 or later. Review RadPersistenceManager and RadDockLayout persistence settings and investigate exposed deployments.
advisories.exploitation: Not confirmed exploited in this vendor bulletin.

advisories.title: Progress Sitefinity improper access control in web services
advisories.summary: Progress Sitefinity web services may disclose restricted content due to improper access controls. Affected deployments may suffer serious confidentiality, integrity and availability impact.
advisories.affected: Sitefinity 15.4.8623 up to but not including 15.4.8630, as detailed in the vendor/CVE record.
advisories.remediation: Upgrade the affected Sitefinity 15.4 release to 15.4.8630 or later. Review vendor security updates for older supported versions.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed exploitation in the cited reference.

sources.label: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security Progress notice

advisories.title: Veeam Backup & Replication CDP Coordinator authorization bypass
advisories.summary: An unauthenticated attacker can bypass authorization in the CDP Coordinator Service on affected Veeam Backup & Replication version 13 deployments.
advisories.affected: Veeam Backup & Replication 13.1.1.18 and earlier 13.1 builds, or 13.0.2.29 and earlier 13.0 builds. Vendor states 12.x is not affected.
advisories.remediation: Install Veeam Backup & Replication 13.1.2.57 or 13.0.3.63, respectively, or a newer fixed build. Validate backup infrastructure exposure.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed exploitation indicated in the cited vendor bulletin.

advisories.title: Managed Veeam Agent for Linux local privilege escalation
advisories.summary: Local privilege escalation in Veeam Agent for Linux, applicable only to installations managed by a Veeam Backup & Replication instance.
advisories.affected: Veeam Agent for Linux 13.1.1.4 and earlier 13.1 builds when managed by Veeam Backup & Replication. Vendor says 13.0.x and 6.x are not affected.
advisories.remediation: Upgrade the managed Veeam Agent for Linux to 13.1.2.11 or later and confirm rollout on protected hosts.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed exploitation indicated in the cited vendor bulletin.

advisories.title: Sophos Firewall Secure PDF eXchange preauthentication code execution
advisories.summary: Arbitrary file writing in Sophos Firewall Secure PDF eXchange can allow remote code execution before authentication when the specified SPX configuration is combined with High Availability mode.
advisories.affected: Sophos Firewall 21.5 GA and earlier. The exploitation prerequisites are limited to specifically configured SPX and HA deployments.
advisories.remediation: Confirm the Sophos hotfix is applied on the supported SFOS version, or upgrade to a version containing the fix (21.0 MR2 or newer per Sophos). Confirm automatic installation of hotfixes is enabled.
advisories.exploitation: Sophos reported no observed exploitation at the time of its July 2025 advisory.

advisories.title: Sophos Firewall legacy SMTP proxy SQL injection leading to code execution
advisories.summary: SQL injection in the legacy transparent SMTP proxy can lead to remote code execution when a quarantining policy is active and the firewall was upgraded from an older SFOS release.
advisories.affected: Sophos Firewall 21.5 GA and older under the vendor-stated SMTP proxy and quarantine prerequisites.
advisories.remediation: Verify the Sophos hotfix has been installed or upgrade to a fixed supported SFOS version. Review the exact appliance configuration and vendor remediation matrix.
advisories.exploitation: Sophos reported no observed exploitation at the time of its July 2025 advisory.

advisories.title: Microsoft Windows Shell security feature bypass affecting Windows 11
advisories.summary: Windows Shell security feature bypass that has been reported exploited. Windows 11 users should apply the appropriate October 2026 security updates for their specific version.
advisories.affected: Applicable Windows 11 versions include 23H2, 24H2, 25H2, 26H1 and 26H2 per Microsoft update applicability; determine the required KB/build for each installed version.
advisories.remediation: Install the applicable October 2026 Windows security cumulative update or newer supported update. Verify Microsoft's Security Update Guide and Windows 11 release-health matrix before deployment.
advisories.exploitation: Reported exploited in the wild; CISA KEV listing should be checked by live feed.

advisories.title: Microsoft Exchange Server SE weak authentication privilege escalation
advisories.summary: Weak authentication in Microsoft Exchange Server may allow an authenticated attacker to elevate privileges over the network. The vulnerability is included in Microsoft Exchange Server Subscription Edition security servicing.
advisories.affected: Exchange Server Subscription Edition RTM builds earlier than 15.2.2562.53 are listed as affected in the published Microsoft/NVD record.
advisories.remediation: Install an applicable current Exchange Server SE security update. Microsoft lists Oct26SU build 15.2.2562.56 for Exchange SE RTM; confirm prerequisites and supported servicing channel before patching.
advisories.exploitation: Active exploitation is not confirmed by the cited Microsoft KB.

advisories.title: .NET Brotli decompression out of bounds write
advisories.summary: An out of bounds memory write in the Brotli decoder used by modern .NET and ASP.NET Core may cause memory corruption, information disclosure, denial of service or privilege elevation when the application decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data. Automatic request/response decompression is disabled by default. On Windows, PHP 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 and 8.2.35-1 package rebuilds include Brotli 1.2.1 to fix this vulnerability in cURL decompression dependencies; it is not an additional PHP language CVE.
advisories.affected: Affected .NET 8 versions earlier than 8.0.33, .NET 9 earlier than 9.0.22, .NET 10 earlier than 10.0.14, and affected .NET 11 prereleases earlier than RC3. Specific NativeAOT and runtime packs vary by platform. Classic .NET Framework is not affected by this CVE. PHP Windows builds without the October 26 -1 Brotli dependency rebuild may carry a vulnerable decoder in the cURL extension when automatic HTTP decompression is enabled.
advisories.remediation: Update affected installations to .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22 or 10.0.14 (or .NET 11 RC3 for prerelease installations). Rebuild self-contained apps and containers with the fixed runtimes, and update affected NuGet packages where the advisory requires it. For affected PHP Windows distributions, install the corresponding PHP 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 or 8.2.35-1 build including Brotli 1.2.1.
advisories.exploitation: CISA KEV added the underlying Google Brotli CVE on October 27, 2026, indicating confirmed exploitation of the vulnerable component. This does not establish exploitation of a .NET deployment or a specific CVEHarbor visitor's application.

advisories.title: .NET Linux tarball ownership privilege escalation
advisories.summary: Incorrect ownership metadata in certain ASP.NET Core Linux runtime and targeting pack tarballs and source-built .NET archives could allow local privilege escalation when extracting affected distributions with unsafe ownership.
advisories.affected: ASP.NET Core 8 and 9 Linux runtime or targeting-pack tarballs before 8.0.33 and 9.0.22. Source-built .NET 8/9/10/11 tarballs have separately listed affected ranges. Ordinary Microsoft-published .NET 10/11 runtime and SDK tarballs are not in scope.
advisories.remediation: Replace affected ASP.NET Core Linux tarballs with corrected 8.0.33 / 9.0.22 distributions, or use patched source-build archives for applicable SDKs. Audit and correct ownership of files already extracted; merely downloading the new archive does not repair existing permissions.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed exploitation in the cited Microsoft advisory.

advisories.title: .NET SocketAsyncEventArgs memory corruption remote code execution
advisories.summary: On Windows, reusing SocketAsyncEventArgs across IPv4 and IPv6 datagram sockets can retain an undersized native address buffer. Untrusted datagrams can trigger an out of bounds memory write. The original October 13 fix was incomplete; Microsoft provided corrected patches October 25.
advisories.affected: Affected .NET 8 prior to 8.0.33, .NET 9 before 9.0.22, .NET 10 before 10.0.14, and affected .NET 11 previews before RC3 on Windows when the vulnerable socket behavior is reachable.
advisories.remediation: Update affected installations to .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22 or 10.0.14 (or .NET 11 RC3 for prerelease installations). Rebuild self-contained apps and containers with the fixed runtimes, and update affected NuGet packages where the advisory requires it. The October 13 releases alone do not fully fix this CVE.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed active exploitation stated in the cited Microsoft security advisory.

advisories.title: ASP.NET Core Blazor WebAssembly debugger code execution
advisories.summary: The Blazor WebAssembly debug proxy may compile attacker-influenced debugger expressions into C# without sufficient escaping, enabling code execution on a developer workstation when a developer evaluates affected data. Microsoft corrected an incomplete October 13 package fix on October 25.
advisories.affected: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server and Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.DevServer 10.x before 10.0.14 and affected .NET 11 prereleases before 11.0.0 RC3. This requires vulnerable debugging activity and is not a general production request endpoint issue.
advisories.remediation: Update both affected Blazor WebAssembly Server and DevServer NuGet packages to 10.0.14 or 11.0.0 RC3 as applicable, and update the development SDK. A shared runtime update alone does not fix independently referenced packages.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed active exploitation stated in the cited Microsoft advisory.

sources.label: Microsoft corrected Blazor debugger security advisory

advisories.title: ASP.NET Core Kestrel HTTP/1 request smuggling
advisories.summary: An aborted Kestrel HTTP/1 connection can cause unread request body data to be reparsed as a new request, allowing HTTP request smuggling or message desynchronization in affected ASP.NET Core hosts.
advisories.affected: Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime versions 8.0.0 through 8.0.31, 9.0.0 through 9.0.20, 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and corresponding affected .NET 11 prereleases.
advisories.remediation: Microsoft first patched in ASP.NET Core 8.0.32, 9.0.21, 10.0.13 and .NET 11 RC2. Prefer the newer 8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14 or RC3 October 25 releases for current servicing.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed exploitation in the cited Microsoft advisory.

sources.label: Microsoft ASP.NET Core Kestrel security advisory

advisories.title: ASP.NET Core HTTP/2 Kestrel request desynchronization
advisories.summary: Kestrel accepts newline characters in HTTP/2 trailers or dynamic HPACK table values when it should reject malformed headers, allowing potential HTTP request desynchronization and a security feature bypass.
advisories.affected: Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime versions 8.0.0 through 8.0.31, 9.0.0 through 9.0.20, 10.0.0 through 10.0.12, and .NET 11 prereleases through RC1.
advisories.remediation: Fixed initially in ASP.NET Core 8.0.32, 9.0.21, 10.0.13 and .NET 11 RC2. Install the newer supported October 25 releases where applicable (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14, RC3).
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed exploitation in the cited Microsoft advisory.

sources.label: Microsoft ASP.NET Core HTTP/2 security advisory

advisories.title: .NET Framework untrusted search path security feature bypass
advisories.summary: Untrusted search path handling in classic Microsoft .NET Framework permits a locally authorized attacker to bypass a security feature. The patch is part of Microsoft's October 2026 .NET Framework cumulative security updates.
advisories.affected: Multiple .NET Framework 3.5, 4.6.2 through 4.8.1 configurations across supported Windows versions, subject to Microsoft update applicability. This is a separate classic .NET Framework CVE, not the modern .NET Brotli issue.
advisories.remediation: Install the correct October 13, 2026 .NET Framework cumulative update or a newer superseding Windows update for the installed Windows and .NET Framework versions. Consult the Microsoft patch matrix for the specific KB.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed active exploitation in the referenced Microsoft advisories.

advisories.title: PHP critical remote code execution via out-of-memory corruption
advisories.summary: Out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Unsafe request cleanup can lead to memory corruption and unauthenticated remote code execution. All web request serving installations require version and exposure checks, with demonstrated risk for Apache mod_php.
advisories.affected: PHP 8.5.0–8.5.11; 8.4.0–8.4.26; 8.3.0–8.3.35; 8.2.0–8.2.34. Older end-of-life branches may also be affected; upstream fixed versions are unavailable for them.
advisories.remediation: Upgrade supported PHP branches to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, respectively. Rebuild and restart affected web workers and containers. PHP 8.1 and older need a supported upgrade or validated distribution backports. PHP says configuration workarounds do not fully mitigate these vulnerabilities.
advisories.exploitation: Confirmed actively exploited: CISA added the CVE to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26, 2026.

advisories.title: PHP critical remote code execution via stale global state
advisories.summary: PHP request-owned internal state may outlive freed memory. A subsequent web request can access that stale state, potentially allowing unauthenticated remote code execution via use-after-free, particularly in affected request initialization and session processing paths.
advisories.affected: PHP 8.5.0–8.5.11; 8.4.0–8.4.26; 8.3.0–8.3.35; 8.2.0–8.2.34. Older end-of-life branches may also be affected; upstream fixed versions are unavailable for them.
advisories.remediation: Upgrade supported PHP branches to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, respectively. Rebuild and restart affected web workers and containers. PHP 8.1 and older need a supported upgrade or validated distribution backports. PHP says configuration workarounds do not fully mitigate these vulnerabilities.
advisories.exploitation: Confirmed actively exploited: CISA added the CVE to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26, 2026.

advisories.title: PHP session upload progress security advisory under unusual configuration
advisories.summary: The PHP project identified an additional potential remote code execution vector involving session upload progress and an unusual sequence: an application configures session.serialize_handler as php_binary or php_serialize, switches it to php at runtime using ini_set, and then calls session_start. This specific issue was not fixed by the October 21 security releases. Vendor rates the circumstance unlikely; no standalone CVSS rating is asserted here.
advisories.affected: PHP installations that enable session.upload_progress and use the unusual runtime session.serialize_handler switching sequence. Affected version ranges and the precise final fixed version await the PHP project's dedicated advisory.
advisories.remediation: Until the dedicated patch is available, set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 in the administrative PHP configuration and restart relevant PHP workers if the feature is not required. Review application behavior. Follow future upstream PHP advisories for the actual fix.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed active exploitation of this separate configuration-dependent issue in the cited PHP announcement.

advisories.title: Angular HTTP Client can leak XSRF tokens through URL parsing discrepancy
advisories.summary: Angular HttpClient's earlier URL parsing fix was incomplete. Carefully crafted cross-origin requests can send an XSRF token to an attacker-controlled endpoint when attack preconditions are met. The Angular project calls this High while the GitHub reviewed database currently lists Moderate; the score is not asserted here.
advisories.affected: @angular/common 21.0.0 to below 21.0.3, 20.0.0 to below 20.3.34, and 19.2.25 or earlier. Angular 19 is outside security support.
advisories.remediation: Upgrade @angular/common to 21.0.3 or later within the 21 branch, or 20.3.34 or later within the 20 branch. Angular 19 deployments should migrate to a supported release. Validate URLs and do not pass untrusted destinations to mutating HttpClient requests.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed exploitation in the cited Angular advisory.

advisories.title: React Server Components unauthenticated remote code execution
advisories.summary: React Server Components can permit remote code execution from specially crafted payloads under rare conditions involving multiple typed arrays and attacker-controlled values. This official upstream advisory currently has no assigned CVE, so it must not be included in unique CVE totals.
advisories.affected: react-server-dom-webpack, react-server-dom-parcel and react-server-dom-turbopack 19.0.0 through 19.0.8, 19.1.0 through 19.1.9, 19.2.0 through 19.2.8 and 19.3.0. Client-only React applications without Server Components are not affected by this issue.
advisories.remediation: Upgrade the affected React Server Components packages to 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9, 19.3.1 or later fixed equivalents, and confirm the related framework's own patch status.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed exploitation asserted by the cited upstream advisory.

advisories.title: React Server Components unauthenticated remote code execution (2025 disclosure)
advisories.summary: Affected React Server Components packages allow an unauthenticated attacker to exploit unsafe deserialization of Server Function requests, potentially leading to remote code execution. This is a historical 2025 advisory, distinct from the October 2026 GHSA-only issue.
advisories.affected: react-server-dom-webpack, react-server-dom-parcel and react-server-dom-turbopack versions 19.0.0, 19.1.0, 19.1.1 and 19.2.0. Client-only React applications that do not use React Server Components are not affected.
advisories.remediation: Upgrade affected packages to 19.0.1, 19.1.2 or 19.2.1 or a later fixed release. If using Next.js, install the corresponding patched Next.js release as documented by its security advisory.
advisories.exploitation: No current exploitation assertion is made here; check CISA KEV and the vendor record before treating exploitation as confirmed.

advisories.title: SharePoint Server SQL injection privilege elevation
advisories.summary: An authenticated attacker can exploit improper neutralization of SQL input in Microsoft Office SharePoint to elevate privileges over the network. This is a SharePoint Server Subscription Edition issue rather than proof of a vulnerability in SharePoint Online.
advisories.affected: SharePoint Server Subscription Edition builds before October 13, 2026 security update 16.0.20326.20190 for affected servicing configurations. Confirm precise applicability with the Microsoft Security Update Guide.
advisories.remediation: Apply Microsoft SharePoint Server Subscription Edition October 13, 2026 security update KB5002927 (build 16.0.20326.20190), or a newer superseding update. If using SharePoint Workflow Manager, first install KB5002799 as Microsoft directs.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed exploitation stated in Microsoft's referenced October security update.

advisories.title: SharePoint Server SSRF information disclosure
advisories.summary: Server-side request forgery in SharePoint Server can allow an authenticated attacker to disclose information across a network. This is not a claim that SharePoint Online tenants have this exposure.
advisories.affected: Microsoft SharePoint Server Subscription Edition 16.0 builds before 16.0.20326.20190 under the affected configuration; confirm patch and applicability with MSRC.
advisories.remediation: Deploy the applicable SharePoint Server security update KB5002927 (build 16.0.20326.20190) or a newer superseding update. Validate Workflow Manager prerequisites.
advisories.exploitation: No confirmed active exploitation in the cited MSRC record.

advisories.title: Kendo UI PDFViewer cross-site scripting
advisories.summary: The Progress Kendo UI and Telerik PDFViewer can execute attacker-controlled JavaScript when an application loads a specially crafted document and a user interacts with functionality that rerenders the DOM. Affected products include Kendo UI for jQuery, Kendo UI for Angular and KendoReact; this does not mean jQuery, Angular or React core is vulnerable.
advisories.affected: Kendo UI for jQuery versions 2024.4.1112 through 2025.2.520, Kendo UI for Angular 18.5.0 through 19.1.2, and KendoReact 5.10.0 through 11.1.0, plus affected Telerik UI PDFViewer products.
advisories.remediation: Upgrade Kendo UI for jQuery to 2025.2.702 or later, Kendo UI for Angular to 19.2.0 or later, and use the corresponding vendor fixed KendoReact/Telerik release. If the PDFViewer component is not used, the described impact does not apply.
advisories.exploitation: No known active exploitation confirmed in the cited vendor advisory.

sources.label: Progress Kendo UI for jQuery official security notice
Progress Kendo UI for Angular notice

advisories.title: MongoDB Server compressed-message heap memory disclosure
advisories.summary: Unauthenticated clients can induce uninitialized heap memory disclosure through inconsistent length fields in compressed MongoDB protocol headers. This vulnerability is in MongoDB Server and may expose secrets, session data or query information.
advisories.affected: MongoDB 8.2 below 8.2.3; 8.0 below 8.0.17; 7.0 below 7.0.28; 6.0 below 6.0.27; 5.0 below 5.0.32; 4.4 below 4.4.30. Older unsupported MongoDB 4.2, 4.0 and 3.6 branches require a supported upgrade.
advisories.remediation: Upgrade to MongoDB 8.2.3, 8.0.17, 7.0.28, 6.0.27, 5.0.32 or 4.4.30 as applicable. If patching is delayed, disable zlib network compression and restrict exposure following the vendor's guidance.
advisories.exploitation: Confirmed exploited: CISA added CVE-2025-14847 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on December 29, 2025.

sources.label: NVD CVE and CISA KEV record
